A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E-CIT research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic conditional-independence experiments, flow-cytometry evaluations, causal-discovery experiments, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds an evaluation of the cd3cd28-only flow-cytometry subset in Table 9.

M1.justification: The data-partitioning procedure, independent subset tests, stable-distribution transformation, and p-value aggregation remain unchanged. The expanded hyperparameter guidance does not introduce a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: Appendix E.4 adds a separate cd3cd28-only evaluation, called Dataset B, alongside the retained pool of cd3cd28 and cd3cd28icam2, now called Dataset A. This adds a single-stimulation evaluation scenario within the existing biological dataset and conditional-independence task, rather than a new data source.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in corresponding experiments are retained. New Table 9 uses the same six CIT methods as Table 3; CCMI is referenced as a benchmark precedent but is not evaluated. FastKCIT remains included in Section 4.1 and excluded from the causal-discovery comparison.

E3.justification: The added Dataset B experiment uses 853 samples with K = 2 and subset size approximately 426, retaining the 50 independent and 50 dependent pairs and existing evaluation metrics. The original 1755-sample experiment with K = 5 remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The stability-parameter sweep, conditioning-dimensionality analysis, subset-size ablation, combination-method comparison, and empirical p-value diagnostics are retained. The new Dataset B table supplies benchmark results; the added discussion of distribution drift does not introduce a robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts, the one-sided 0.1 significance convention, and Figure 3's standard-deviation reporting are unchanged. Real-data averaging remains 10 runs for E-CIT and 100 for RCIT and its ensemble. Expanded table captions explain significance markings already present in v1.

E6.justification: V2 adds precision, recall, and F1 results for Dataset B in Table 9. For example, original/ensemble F1 is 0.759/0.747 for KCIT and 0.766/0.778 for LPCIT. These are additional results under a different configuration, not changes to the retained Table 3 scores. Existing numerical tables and plotted findings are retained.

T1.justification: The definitions, propositions, consistency conditions, and proofs retain their mathematical substance. V2 makes exact p-values and independence more explicit, but these requirements already appear in v1's definitions, validity proof, and Appendix F. Other proof edits concern wording or notation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a general divide-and-aggregate CIT framework, linear sample-size complexity for fixed subset size, conditional statistical guarantees, and competitive empirical performance. The revised discussion reiterates these contributions without adding a new principal scientific claim.

C2.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F newly emphasize that E-CIT does not solve the curse of dimensionality and that distribution drift can invalidate its i.i.d. assumptions. Appendix E.4 also adds a causal explanation for treating the selected stimulation data as observational: interventions affect unobserved exogenous roots while preserving downstream structure.

D1.justification: Appendix E.4 identifies the biological conditions composing the original dataset and documents the added subset's partition settings. It also replaces the original pool's rough subset-size description of approximately 400 with approximately 351, consistent with the unchanged 1755 samples and K = 5; this does not establish changed partitioning.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wang et al. (2025) on practical kernel selection while retaining the median-bandwidth protocol. Section 3.2 also sharpens the structural positioning: E-CIT generalizes Stouffer's combination, whereas Ling and Rho generalize the Liu–Xie and Liptak approaches. The broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language corrections, expands Section 5 into labeled discussions of scope, implementation, and limitations, and rewrites Appendix E.4 for clarity. It adds acknowledgments and publication/author information and corrects the causal-discovery appendix cross-reference. Most document organization and prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and Figure 2 uses tighter Type I error axes with an explicit 0.05 reference line. V2 adds Table 9, expands significance legends, and adjusts table sizing and placement. The previous combination-method Table 9 is retained as Table 10.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through clearer applicability limits, more precise flow-cytometry configuration details, and an additional comparison showing mixed ensemble benefits. Figure 2 also makes deviations from nominal Type I error easier to assess. These are useful, limited gains in documentation and evidential balance; the core method, proofs, and existing results remain essentially unchanged.
